cohort: 29,807 pregnant women who delivered in Lianyungang, Jiangsu Province, eastern China, between July 1, 2021 and June 30, 2022
finding: The incidence of preterm birth was 5.1% and was associated with several factors, including young and advanced maternal age, cesarean section delivery, multiple perinatal births, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, placenta previa, and a history of preterm birth.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with an increased risk of preterm birth.
